label: early copy-phase steps (recalling original tokens 1-2), sparse
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the first two copy inputs after <DEL> (input = orig(0) or orig(1), output = orig(1) or orig(2)); recall_idx 1-2 hold ~88% of activation mass, with a small tail at recall_idx 3 and at the final steps of L=9 sequences. Never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on the first occurrence of a token. Even within that window it fires on only ~5% of steps: rate is higher for long sequences (L=8-9) and for input tokens x, 3, o, l (top activations are almost all x/o/3/l fed back), and somewhat for next outputs 0/1/q/b, but no simple token or context rule gives high precision (best F1 found ~0.30 with in_tok in {x,3,o,l} and L>=8). Magnitude is largest when the copied input is x, o, 3 or l at recall_idx 1-2.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: x, 3, o, l; t=12: x, 3, o, l; t=13: x, 3, l, o) and the next token to output (most: 1, 0, b, q, e, y; least: l, r, -, o); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=3 & t=4, t=17.
